bull.b: Growing cloud revenue and a rising share from production applications indicate customers are moving beyond experimentation toward recurring operational use. This supports a more durable services model, strengthens customer integration, and can improve revenue visibility as deployments expand.

The sharp increase in bookings and remaining performance obligations provides contracted demand that can support revenue over the next several quarters. A larger backlog also validates commercial traction and gives the company a foundation for scaling customer implementations and system deliveries.

Peer-reviewed hardware validation combined with established annealing capabilities gives D-Wave exposure to multiple quantum-computing approaches. This platform breadth may widen its addressable applications, support ecosystem development, and improve competitive resilience as customer workloads evolve.

bear.b: Large and worsening operating losses show that commercial progress has not yet produced an economically self-sustaining business. Continued cash consumption can restrict strategic flexibility, increase reliance on external funding, and make execution more sensitive to delays in scaling revenue.

Dependence on occasional system sales creates uneven revenue recognition and makes comparisons highly sensitive to delivery and installation timing. This volatility complicates planning, reduces near-term visibility, and leaves results exposed when large customer deployments shift between reporting periods.

Higher personnel and development spending may support future product capability, but it is currently widening operating losses before the related investments generate sufficient revenue. The burden raises the execution threshold for the roadmap and could prolong dependence on financing while growth initiatives mature.
